subject.title: [Bug]: Teams app removal/re-add retains prior DM session history

question: For true Microsoft Teams app-management removal, should OpenClaw isolate future DMs by rotating/staling the route-matched session and removing the cached Teams conversation reference without deleting transcript files?
rationale: The source fix is concrete, but the behavior controls personal-chat history retention and proactive conversation reachability after app removal, so automation should not choose the privacy boundary alone.

options.title: Use non-destructive reset plus reference removal
options.body: Treat observable Teams app removal as a session boundary, clear the proactive conversation reference, and preserve transcript files unless a separate retention policy changes that.

options.title: Require stronger deletion semantics
options.body: Pause the linked PRs until app removal deletes or archives retained Teams DM transcript/session data under an explicit data-retention policy.

options.title: Reject server-side lifecycle resets
options.body: Close the linked implementation work and document app-removal/session retention as outside OpenClaw's supported Teams boundary.

recommendation.title: Use non-destructive reset plus reference removal
recommendation.body: Treat observable Teams app removal as a session boundary, clear the proactive conversation reference, and preserve transcript files unless a separate retention policy changes that.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent Teams state-store and security-sensitive history for deciding the retained-history boundary.
